correctness.rationale: Cameron--Gewurz--Merola's product-action formalism gives all-tuple orbit count F_n^d and inverse Stirling transform for distinct tuples; weak orders give the same model directly. For d>=3, a prescribed pair is tied in all coordinates with probability (F_{n-1}/F_n)^d, so the expected number of common-tie pairs is asymptotic to (log 2)^d n^(2-d)/2. Any two distinct pair events, overlapping or disjoint, collapse exactly two degrees of freedom and have probability (F_{n-2}/F_n)^d; summing O(n^4) such intersections is o(n^(2-d)). Bonferroni therefore gives the stated first deficit. A fresh exact Stirling replay through n=80 produced scaled deficits approaching the constants for d=3,4,5. The d=2 constant is the prior incidence-matrix asymptotic.
risks: Dimension d is fixed as n tends to infinity; no uniform growing-d regime is proved.

final_claim: For the d-fold ordered full product, the injective-to-all ordered-tuple orbit ratio has a dimension-two collision transition: it tends to exp(-(log 2)^2/2) for d=2, while for every fixed d>=3 its deficit is asymptotic to (log 2)^d/(2 n^(d-2)).
limitations: Exact product-action formulas and d=2 asymptotic are prior work.
